semantics: Binary.parseComponent, then Comp.denI over Binary.coreModSemI P: each core module decoded and run on the Core 3.0 engine at profile P, its start function at instantiation; core instances instantiated in program order (the reading of componentBytesSystemCore3I P before its export phase)
assumptions: existence: one play at every profile P
exclusion: every finite play at every deterministic profile profile o (every GrowOracle o)
divergence is not observed: a start function or export call that never returns makes no move
typed host: f is answered () (unitHost); the import-call clauses hold whatever the host answers
no async, resources, streams or futures (the lowering rejects them)

binaries.name: starts
core_instances: glob: start function writes 42 into a global (initially 0); exports get, which reads it
binaries.strength: proved (kernel-checked): the play [inst, f(1), (), f(2), (), ready, get(), 42] at every profile; at every deterministic profile every play's host calls are a prefix of f(1), f(2), a complete instantiation under the typed host is exactly that trace then ready, and every answer to get() is 42

ref.strength: one executed reference-machine run (decide +kernel on its drivers) on the component Conformance.decodeRef reads from these bytes (kernel_rfl; validated by check?): host log f(1), f(2); get() returns 42. Example agreement only, not a general binary-to-REF equivalence

bridge.strength: structural, proved for every binary (DecoderBridge.rel_of_decode): when Binary.parseComponent and Conformance.decodeRef both succeed, they read the same Binary.parse AST and agree on core instantiations (the same core modules, decoded from the same bytes, instantiated in the same order); this binary is an instance

bridge_wiring.strength: wiring and types, proved for every binary whose REF reading is in the decidable fragment DecoderBridge.InFrag (DecoderBridge.relW_of_decode): the IR's imports, exports (names, types, lift/lower chains) and each node's module interface and wiring are those the reference component's definitions name, resolved as the reference machine resolves names (DecoderBridge.refRead); this binary is in the fragment (starts_inFrag, decide +kernel). Syntax only: that the reference machine's run follows refRead is not proved

binaries.bridge_semantic: open: behavioural adequacy of Comp.denI against the reference machine is the open goal DecoderBridge.Task.startAdequacyChecked (this binary is an instance of it: DecoderBridge.starts_of, with DecoderBridge.starts_rootChecked; the unrestricted DecoderBridge.Task.startAdequacy is false, see the regression paramname); this binary is import-wired (DecoderBridge.starts_hostWired), so the instantiation part of every such IR play is node by node (DecoderBridge.nodesInst_of_startPlay, proved); its first core node is in the decidable fragment FirstImpFrag (DecoderBridge.starts_firstImpFrag: the module call1 imports exactly the canon lower of f), on which the reference half of a first node that is ready after host calls t is proved up to the return of its start function (DecoderBridge.firstImp_ready_ref); it is in the decidable fragment MultiImpFrag (DecoderBridge.starts_multiImpFrag), on which Task.startAdequacy is reduced to the export call (DecoderBridge.startAdequacyFrag_of_nodes): the IR's node calls (DecoderBridge.nodeCallsIR) and the whole reference instantiation (DecoderBridge.nodesRef: the first node with its start epilogue, the two later nodes call2 and glob in the shared core store, each node's IR store mapped into it with its imports kept at the trampoline, then the remaining definitions and the end of the instantiation) are proved, the export call (Task.exportRef) is open; DecoderBridge.starts_of_d derives the reference half of this binary from its IR run given Task.exportRef, and the agreement on this binary rests on executing both machines only

binaries.name: trap
core_instances: trap: start function is unreachable; exports get (returns 7)
call2: start function would call f(2)
binaries.strength: proved (kernel-checked): the play [inst, fail ()] at every profile; at every deterministic profile every play is a prefix of it (plus at most one unanswered Opponent move): never ready, no host call (f(2) never runs), no export answered, export phase empty

ref.strength: one executed reference-machine run on the component Conformance.decodeRef reads from these bytes (kernel_rfl; validated by check?): the instantiation traps. Example agreement only, not a general binary-to-REF equivalence

bridge.strength: structural, proved for every binary (DecoderBridge.rel_of_decode): when Binary.parseComponent and Conformance.decodeRef both succeed, they read the same Binary.parse AST and agree on core instantiations (the same core modules, decoded from the same bytes, instantiated in the same order); this binary is an instance

bridge_wiring.strength: wiring and types, proved for every binary whose REF reading is in the decidable fragment DecoderBridge.InFrag (DecoderBridge.relW_of_decode): the IR's imports, exports (names, types, lift/lower chains) and each node's module interface and wiring are those the reference component's definitions name, resolved as the reference machine resolves names (DecoderBridge.refRead); this binary is in the fragment (trap_inFrag, decide +kernel). Syntax only: that the reference machine's run follows refRead is not proved

binaries.bridge_semantic: open: behavioural adequacy of Comp.denI against the reference machine is the open goal DecoderBridge.Task.failAdequacy (this binary is an instance of it: DecoderBridge.trap_of); on import-wired binaries, this one included (DecoderBridge.trap_hostWired), its IR half is proved and it reduces to the reference half DecoderBridge.Task.failRefWired (DecoderBridge.failAdequacyWired_of), whose first-node case is proved on the decidable fragment FirstCoreFrag (DecoderBridge.firstCore_fail_ref; this binary is in it, trap_firstCoreFrag), so the reference trap of this binary is derived from its IR run without executing the reference machine (DecoderBridge.trap_of_firstCore); the case of a first module importing canon lower trampolines is proved too (DecoderBridge.firstImp_fail_ref, fragment FirstImpFrag), and the remaining cases DecoderBridge.Task.failRefWiredRest' are open

regressions.name: instexport
regressions.what: an exported instance: the core get (returning 42) is lifted and exported through an inline instance i; the component also imports f: func(x: u32), unused

facts.statement: the IR reading (Binary.parseComponent) is instExportComp; its only export is named i#get (instExport_ir_exports)
the REF reading (Conformance.decodeRef) is instExportRef, which exports the instance i; it is valid (instExport_valid) and not in the fragment InFrag (instExport_not_inFrag)
an executed reference run (logging host, hostConfigX, decide +kernel on instantiateRun) instantiates it with no function export, so the lookup of i#get fails on that run

regressions.status: demonstrated mismatch of the two readings' export names (kernel runs), not a disproof of the first statement of Task.startAdequacy (the IR's answer to i#get and the absence of i#get from every reference run are not proved); excluded by the fragment hypothesis InFrag now in Task.startAdequacy; comparing instance-exported functions needs a reference export-path lookup, which is open

regressions.name: paramname
regressions.what: starts with the import declared f: func(y: u32) instead of f: func(x: u32); the binary differs from starts.wasm in that one byte

facts.statement: the IR reading (Binary.parseComponent) is startsComp: parameter names are dropped, so the IR plays are those of starts.wasm
the REF reading (Conformance.decodeRef) is paramNameRef, valid (paramName_valid) and in InFrag (paramName_inFrag)
the root certificate RootChecked (the reference machine's own root checks against the host f: func(x: u32)) rejects it; starts.wasm passes it (starts_rootChecked)
no reference run (logging host, hostConfigX, first.prof) finishes the instantiation; it traps (paramName_traps)

regressions.status: counterexample proved: Task.startAdequacy is false; corrected goal Task.startAdequacyChecked (hypothesis RootChecked, open); outside RootChecked the reference instantiation traps and has no run (traps_of_not_rootChecked, not_instantiates_of_not_rootChecked); MultiImpFrag passes RootChecked (rootChecked_of_multiImpFrag)
